Way at the top of the thread, I was showing off and did some flamenco with a very wonderful guitar. So, my head is sort of still in the flamenco mode, so I'm not sure how well any recommendations will come out.

Uncle John's Band and Friend of the Devil are both fun Grateful Dead songs, and are good for getting your fingers limbered up and used to moving into a few positions. If I had a student, I'd recommend both because I'd want to teach them how to do the G chord with middle, ring, and pinky fingers. This will teach them greater finger dexterity and get them used to using all four of their fingers, as they'd still make the C chord with the first three fingers. It's a good skill to learn and great for dexterity.

There's also Knocking On Heavens Door or Mr. Tambourine Man from Bob Dylan, though All Along The Watchtower is fun, as well. For fun, you can switch between Dylan's way and Hendrix's power chords in the middle and just have fun jamming on it. It's largely played with the pentatonic scale on the 7th fret when Hendrix is soloing. It's fine on an acoustic and good to practice some bends.

There's a chordal version of Johnny I Hardly Knew Ye that's a good choice - and I believe that'd really, really suit your singing. It's something you could make your own. There's many variations on the song, but I'd suspect you'd do well with making it your own and somewhere close to a version done by a fella named Benjamin Luxon. In fact, I bet that'd be awesome. You can look at some of the chords and make it your own and really enjoy the vocal work.
